title: Ecosystem Interactions and Dynamics Core Test
description: Core practice for food webs, ecosystem interactions, resources, population patterns, and matter cycling.

questions.prompt: A pond has algae, insects, small fish, and herons. Which part is a producer?
questions.questionText: A pond has algae, insects, small fish, and herons. Which part is a producer?
questions.correctAnswer: algae
questions.explanation: Algae can make sugars using photosynthesis, so they are producers.

questions.prompt: Which interaction is competition?
questions.questionText: Which interaction is competition?
options: two organisms needing the same limited resource
questions.correctAnswer: two organisms needing the same limited resource
questions.explanation: Competition happens when organisms need the same limited resource.

questions.prompt: A drought lowers pond water levels. Insects that need shallow plants decrease. What is the best first cause in the chain?
questions.questionText: A drought lowers pond water levels. Insects that need shallow plants decrease. What is the best first cause in the chain?
questions.correctAnswer: less available water and habitat
questions.explanation: The drought changes a nonliving factor: water and habitat availability.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows energy flow?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows energy flow?
questions.correctAnswer: grass -> rabbit -> fox
questions.explanation: Energy flows from producers to consumers through feeding relationships.

questions.prompt: What happens to many populations when a needed resource becomes limited?
questions.questionText: What happens to many populations when a needed resource becomes limited?
options: competition may increase and some populations may decrease
energy begins cycling exactly like matter
questions.correctAnswer: competition may increase and some populations may decrease
questions.explanation: Limited resources can increase competition and limit population size.

questions.prompt: A food web shows mice eaten by snakes and hawks. If mice decrease sharply, which claim is reasonable?
questions.questionText: A food web shows mice eaten by snakes and hawks. If mice decrease sharply, which claim is reasonable?
options: Snakes and hawks may have less food available.
Snakes and hawks must both increase immediately.
Mice are not connected to the food web.
questions.correctAnswer: Snakes and hawks may have less food available.
questions.explanation: A decrease in prey can reduce food available to predators.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports mutualism?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports mutualism?
options: Bees get nectar from flowers while flowers receive pollen transfer.
Two plants need the same sunlight.
A fish hides under a rock.
questions.correctAnswer: Bees get nectar from flowers while flowers receive pollen transfer.
questions.explanation: Mutualism is an interaction where both organisms benefit.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Only predators matter in ecosystems." Which evidence best challenges the claim?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Only predators matter in ecosystems." Which evidence best challenges the claim?
options: Producers capture energy, decomposers recycle matter, and many organisms interact.
Food webs can be drawn with arrows.
questions.correctAnswer: Producers capture energy, decomposers recycle matter, and many organisms interact.
questions.explanation: Ecosystems depend on many roles, not predators alone.

questions.prompt: A table shows rabbit population rises, then fox population rises later. Which explanation best fits?
questions.questionText: A table shows rabbit population rises, then fox population rises later. Which explanation best fits?
options: More rabbits may provide more food for foxes, allowing foxes to increase later.
Predator and prey populations cannot affect each other.
questions.correctAnswer: More rabbits may provide more food for foxes, allowing foxes to increase later.
questions.explanation: Predator populations can respond after prey availability changes.

questions.prompt: Which arrow direction in a food web is most useful for showing energy transfer?
questions.questionText: Which arrow direction in a food web is most useful for showing energy transfer?
options: from food source to organism that eats it
from larger organism to smaller organism always
questions.correctAnswer: from food source to organism that eats it
questions.explanation: Food-web arrows usually show the direction energy moves as one organism eats another.

questions.prompt: An invasive plant grows quickly and blocks sunlight from native plants. Which chain is most likely?
questions.questionText: An invasive plant grows quickly and blocks sunlight from native plants. Which chain is most likely?
options: less light for natives -> fewer native plants -> less food for some insects
more shade -> more sunlight -> more native plants
questions.correctAnswer: less light for natives -> fewer native plants -> less food for some insects
questions.explanation: The invasive plant changes light availability, which can ripple to plants and insects.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports that a population is limited by food?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports that a population is limited by food?
options: When seed supply decreases, finch survival and population size decrease.
questions.correctAnswer: When seed supply decreases, finch survival and population size decrease.
questions.explanation: A matching decrease in food and population supports food limitation.

questions.prompt: Which organism role helps return matter from dead organisms to the ecosystem?
questions.questionText: Which organism role helps return matter from dead organisms to the ecosystem?
questions.correctAnswer: decomposer
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead material and return matter to the ecosystem.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Matter disappears when organisms are eaten." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Matter disappears when organisms are eaten." What is the best correction?
options: Matter is transferred and eventually cycled through organisms and the environment.
Food webs do not involve matter.
questions.correctAnswer: Matter is transferred and eventually cycled through organisms and the environment.
questions.explanation: Matter is conserved and moves through living and nonliving parts of ecosystems.

questions.prompt: Which question would best investigate competition between two plant species?
questions.questionText: Which question would best investigate competition between two plant species?
options: Do both species grow less when planted together with limited light?
Which species has a shorter name?
Can either plant be drawn in a diagram?
Does the pot have a label?
questions.correctAnswer: Do both species grow less when planted together with limited light?
questions.explanation: A fair investigation would test whether sharing a limited resource affects growth.

questions.prompt: A food web model leaves out decomposers. What important process is missing?
questions.questionText: A food web model leaves out decomposers. What important process is missing?
options: matter being returned from dead organisms and wastes
questions.correctAnswer: matter being returned from dead organisms and wastes
questions.explanation: Decomposers are important for matter cycling.

questions.prompt: A wetland with many plant species loses one plant species after disease. Insects still have other food sources. What idea does this support?
questions.questionText: A wetland with many plant species loses one plant species after disease. Insects still have other food sources. What idea does this support?
options: only one species is ever important
plants are not part of ecosystems
questions.correctAnswer: biodiversity can help ecosystem stability
questions.explanation: More species can provide alternate pathways and resources when one species changes.

questions.prompt: Which claim is best supported by data showing fewer flowers, fewer bees, and fewer fruits in the same area?
questions.questionText: Which claim is best supported by data showing fewer flowers, fewer bees, and fewer fruits in the same area?
options: Changes in one interaction can affect several populations.
questions.correctAnswer: Changes in one interaction can affect several populations.
questions.explanation: The pattern suggests connected populations through pollination and food-web relationships.

questions.prompt: Which model revision would improve a chain that says drought -> fish decrease?
questions.questionText: Which model revision would improve a chain that says drought -> fish decrease?
options: drought -> less water and shelter -> fewer insects and hiding places -> fish decrease
drought -> fish turn into plants -> fish decrease
drought -> no resources affected -> fish decrease
questions.correctAnswer: drought -> less water and shelter -> fewer insects and hiding places -> fish decrease
questions.explanation: A stronger model shows the intermediate causes that connect drought to fish populations.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why ecosystems are systems?
questions.questionText: Which statement best explains why ecosystems are systems?
options: Living and nonliving parts interact, and a change in one part can affect others.
Every organism lives alone without resources.
Only animals count as ecosystem parts.
questions.correctAnswer: Living and nonliving parts interact, and a change in one part can affect others.
questions.explanation: Systems have interacting parts; ecosystems include organisms and nonliving factors.

questions.prompt: A new predator enters an island ecosystem. Which evidence would best show its effect?
questions.questionText: A new predator enters an island ecosystem. Which evidence would best show its effect?
options: prey population data before and after the predator arrives
the color of the island map
the number of pages in a notebook
questions.correctAnswer: prey population data before and after the predator arrives
questions.explanation: Before-and-after prey data can provide evidence about the predator's effect.

questions.prompt: Which scenario best shows resource competition?
questions.questionText: Which scenario best shows resource competition?
options: Two bird species nesting in the same limited tree cavities
A plant using sunlight to make sugars
questions.correctAnswer: Two bird species nesting in the same limited tree cavities
questions.explanation: The birds compete because they need the same limited nesting sites.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best connects producers to consumers?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best connects producers to consumers?
options: Producers store energy in food molecules that consumers obtain by eating organisms.
questions.correctAnswer: Producers store energy in food molecules that consumers obtain by eating organisms.
questions.explanation: Consumers depend directly or indirectly on producers for food molecules.

questions.prompt: A student sees fewer frogs after pesticide reduces insects. Which claim best uses evidence?
questions.questionText: A student sees fewer frogs after pesticide reduces insects. Which claim best uses evidence?
options: Frogs may have decreased because their food supply decreased.
Frogs decreased because sunlight became louder.
Insects are never connected to frogs.
questions.correctAnswer: Frogs may have decreased because their food supply decreased.
questions.explanation: A decrease in insect prey can affect frog populations.

questions.prompt: Which result would weaken the claim that wolves caused a deer population decrease?
questions.questionText: Which result would weaken the claim that wolves caused a deer population decrease?
options: Deer decreased before wolves arrived and during a severe drought.
Wolves and deer live in the same region.
The deer population was measured every year.
questions.correctAnswer: Deer decreased before wolves arrived and during a severe drought.
questions.explanation: If deer decreased before wolves arrived, another factor such as drought may better explain the pattern.

questions.prompt: Which model best connects matter and energy in ecosystems?
questions.questionText: Which model best connects matter and energy in ecosystems?
options: matter cycles through organisms and decomposers; energy flows through feeding relationships
energy cycles exactly like matter forever
food webs show no energy transfer
questions.correctAnswer: matter cycles through organisms and decomposers; energy flows through feeding relationships
questions.explanation: Matter cycles, while energy flows through food webs and changes form.

questions.prompt: A class removes leaf litter from one soil container but not another. Decomposer numbers drop in the no-litter container. Which explanation fits?
questions.questionText: A class removes leaf litter from one soil container but not another. Decomposer numbers drop in the no-litter container. Which explanation fits?
options: Decomposers lost a food source and habitat material.
questions.correctAnswer: Decomposers lost a food source and habitat material.
questions.explanation: Leaf litter provides dead matter that decomposers use.

questions.prompt: Which management choice best protects ecosystem stability in a restored meadow?
questions.questionText: Which management choice best protects ecosystem stability in a restored meadow?
options: planting several native plant species that support different insects
adding only one food source for all organisms
questions.correctAnswer: planting several native plant species that support different insects
questions.explanation: Native plant diversity can support more interactions and stability.

questions.prompt: A graph shows algae increase after fertilizer runoff, then oxygen levels drop and fish decrease. Which chain best explains the pattern?
questions.questionText: A graph shows algae increase after fertilizer runoff, then oxygen levels drop and fish decrease. Which chain best explains the pattern?
options: extra nutrients -> algae bloom -> decomposition uses oxygen -> fish have less oxygen
extra nutrients -> fish make oxygen -> algae disappear
fertilizer -> sunlight stops -> fish become producers
questions.correctAnswer: extra nutrients -> algae bloom -> decomposition uses oxygen -> fish have less oxygen
questions.explanation: Nutrient pollution can trigger algae blooms and oxygen changes that affect fish.

questions.prompt: Which final explanation best shows ecosystem understanding?
questions.questionText: Which final explanation best shows ecosystem understanding?
options: Ecosystems have interacting living and nonliving parts; resources, feeding relationships, and matter cycling can make one change ripple through many populations.
Ecosystems are lists of animals with no relationships.
Food webs show that matter disappears.
questions.correctAnswer: Ecosystems have interacting living and nonliving parts; resources, feeding relationships, and matter cycling can make one change ripple through many populations.
questions.explanation: This explanation connects systems, resources, food webs, matter cycling, and ripple effects.
